title: Amaravati
subtitle: A capital raised on pooled farmland. Then both lenders left, five days apart.
summary: Andhra Pradesh pooled 33,000 acres from 2,903 farming families for a greenfield capital, backed by $300 million from the World Bank and $200 million from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. India withdrew the World Bank request in July 2019 as an Inspection Panel investigation closed in, the AIIB left five days later, and the site sat frozen for five years with only the High Court finished.
lesson: Development finance sells money and scrutiny as one package; refusing the scrutiny forfeits the money and leaves the findings unaddressed.
locationRole: Greenfield capital city site on the Krishna

title: Buran
subtitle: One flawless unmanned flight. Then a hangar roof fell on it.
summary: The Soviet answer to the Space Shuttle cost 17.8 to 20 billion roubles and flew once, on 15 November 1988, completing two orbits and an automated landing with nobody aboard. Russia cancelled the programme in June 1993, and on 12 May 2002 the roof of the storage hangar at Baikonur collapsed onto the orbiter, destroying it and killing eight workers.
lesson: A demonstration nobody can afford to repeat is not a capability; budget for the operating decade, not the first flight.
locationRole: Launch site and assembly hangar

title: Dawei Special Economic Zone
subtitle: Myanmar's road to the Indian Ocean. Eighteen years on, nothing is built.
summary: Myanmar and Thailand agreed in 2008 to build a 250 square kilometre deep-sea port and industrial complex, costed at $58 billion with an $8.6 billion first phase led by Italian-Thai Development. The coal plant was cancelled in 2012, all seven concessions were terminated in January 2021, and by August 2026 the military was burning villages to clear land for a Russian-backed revival.
lesson: A zone resting on one anchor developer and one foreign partner has no fallback the moment either loses interest.
locationRole: Deep-sea port and industrial zone site

title: The Hazaribagh tannery relocation
subtitle: Tk 1,078 crore moved the tanneries. They were 6% of the river's problem.
summary: Between 2003 and 2017 Bangladesh spent Tk 1,078 crore moving roughly 250 leather tanneries out of central Dhaka to a new estate at Hemayetpur in Savar, to stop chrome discharge into the Buriganga River. Analysis afterwards found the tanneries accounted for only 6% of the river's pollution load, and the relocated estate discharged into the Dhaleshwari instead.
lesson: Measure each source's share before buying the remedy; the most visible polluter is not always the material one.
locationRole: Original tannery district on the Buriganga

title: The Diovan trials
subtitle: Five universities showed the drug did more. A company man supplied the numbers.
summary: From 2002 five Japanese medical schools published trials showing valsartan prevented strokes, angina and heart failure beyond its blood-pressure effect, turning Diovan into a blockbuster in Japan. A Novartis statistician had passed falsified analyses to the researchers; the Lancet and European Heart Journal papers were retracted and Tokyo prosecutors charged both the man and the company in July 2014.
lesson: A sponsor's employee inside the analysis is a conflict, not a courtesy; who touched the data matters as much as the data.
locationRole: Trial site and seat of the prosecution

title: Evergrande
subtitle: A million and a half families paid for homes that were never built.
summary: Founded in 1996, Evergrande became the world's most indebted property developer, running over 1,300 projects across more than 280 cities on money taken from buyers before construction started. Beijing's 2020 leverage caps cut off refinancing, and the company defaulted in December 2021 carrying $305 billion of debt, of which $207 billion was owed to 1.4 million pre-sale homebuyers.
lesson: Customer prepayments are debt with a construction schedule attached; booking them as revenue hides the day the sales stop.
locationRole: Corporate headquarters

title: Forest City
subtitle: Built for 700,000 people on four artificial islands. About 9,000 came.
summary: Country Garden began Forest City in 2006 on four reclaimed islands off southwestern Johor, a roughly $100 billion development marketed as housing for 700,000 residents. Malaysia's restriction on foreign residency and the developer's 2023 bond defaults left about 8,000 to 9,000 people living there against 15% of construction complete, and its international school closed in July 2026.
lesson: A development sold to foreign buyers depends on the host country's residency policy, which is never yours to control.
locationRole: Reclaimed islands in the Johor Strait

title: Yung Drung
subtitle: A Silicon Valley city state, licensed by Bhutan and disowned nine months later.
summary: In 2021 the entrepreneur Art Finch, backed by Pronomos Capital, proposed an autonomous charter city across roughly 2,500 square kilometres of Gelephu, raising $1 million in seed funding and letters of intent worth over $2 billion. Bhutan licensed the venture in 2022, publicly disavowed it in April 2023, and that December announced its own $100 billion Gelephu Mindfulness City on the same land.
lesson: Asking a state to cede jurisdiction may win a licence, but the host can adopt the idea and keep the sovereignty.
locationRole: Proposed special administrative region

title: Bhutan's Education City
subtitle: A billion-dollar knowledge campus. The site ended up mining bitcoin.
summary: Approved by cabinet in 2010 after a $9 million McKinsey study, Education City was a $1 billion, 1,000-acre campus meant to give Bhutan a health, finance and ICT hub. Land tenure disputes and a contractor with no relevant expertise stalled it, the project was cancelled by 2015, and from December 2021 the cleared site was reused for state bitcoin mining.
lesson: A consultant's report cannot supply absorptive capacity; check who at home will actually run the thing before funding it.
locationRole: Abandoned campus site, later a mining farm

title: The Fifth Generation Computer Project
subtitle: Japan bet a decade on logic programming while the world went statistical.
summary: From 1982 Japan's Institute for New Generation Computing Technology spent about 50 billion yen building knowledge-based machines around Prolog, drawing researchers from NEC, Hitachi, Fujitsu and Mitsubishi Electric. International research moved toward statistical and connectionist methods, ICOT's mandate left no room to change course, and the project closed in 1992 with no commercially viable system.
lesson: Concentrated national funding locks in the paradigm it was written for; put the exit into the mandate, not just the milestones.
locationRole: ICOT headquarters

title: Zhuhai Tram Line 1
subtitle: Catenary free, two years late, three and a half years open, then torn up.
summary: Zhuhai built an 8.98 kilometre, 14-station tram line using AnsaldoBreda's catenary-free Sirio system, opening in June 2017 after nearly two years of delay. Breakdowns were frequent and ridership stayed under 3,000 journeys a day against a viability threshold of 5,000 to 10,000; services were suspended in January 2021 and the tracks were dismantled from May 2024.
lesson: A novel system removes the fallback: when the only line stops, riders switch to something else and do not come back.
locationRole: Tram corridor through central Zhuhai

title: The Sanzhi UFO Houses
subtitle: A pod resort on the Taiwan coast that never took a single guest.
summary: The Hung Kuo Group began building a cluster of Futuro-style fibreglass pods on Taiwan's northern coast in 1978, aimed at American military personnel on leave in East Asia. Fatal accidents during construction and mounting losses stopped work in 1980, a 1989 revival died on earthquake safety findings, and the pods were demolished between December 2008 and 2010.
lesson: Novel construction inherits none of the code history that makes ordinary building certifiable; confirm it can pass before you pour.
locationRole: Abandoned pod resort site

title: Hotel New World
subtitle: Six storeys came down in a minute. A draughtsman had drawn the structure.
summary: The six-storey Lian Yak Building, holding the 67-room Hotel New World, collapsed without warning at 12:47pm on 15 March 1986, killing 33 people. The Commission of Inquiry reported in February 1987 that the structural drawings had been produced by an unqualified draughtsman with no professional engineering review, and Singapore ordered inspections of 170 buildings from the same hands.
lesson: A qualification requirement is only a control if someone checks it before approval; the inquiry afterwards is not one.
locationRole: Collapse site at Serangoon and Owen Roads

title: The International Center for Boundary Cooperation
subtitle: A visa-free Eurasian city on the Chinese border. It became a discount mall.
summary: Opened in December 2011 as a visa-free zone straddling the Kazakhstan-China border, the centre was planned with an airport, hotels, casinos, a theme park and a foreign-language university, sized for 30,000 visitors a day. By 2015 it drew roughly 1,500 a day, the Kazakh side was largely an empty dirt lot with vacated vendor stalls, and none of the promised amenities were built.
lesson: Removing a border formality does not manufacture demand; the traffic has to exist before the resorts are worth building.
locationRole: Cross-border free-trade zone

title: The Bank of Bombay
subtitle: It lent the cotton boom everything it had. Then American cotton came back.
summary: Chartered on 15 April 1840 as India's second presidency bank, the Bank of Bombay extended heavy credit to cotton merchants during the shortage caused by the American Civil War. American shipments resumed in 1866, prices collapsed, the bank suspended payments that June, and liquidation from January 1868 wrote off about 1.89 crore rupees of shareholder capital.
lesson: Lending into a supply shock means underwriting its end; price in the day the interrupted competitor returns.
locationRole: Bank headquarters in the Fort district

title: Cheay Areng Dam
subtitle: Villagers held the access road for eleven months. The dam was never begun.
summary: Sinohydro pursued a 108 MW dam on the Areng River in the Cardamom Mountains that would have flooded forest supporting roughly 1,500 indigenous Chorng people. From March 2014 villagers blockaded the access checkpoint for about eleven months, and in January 2015 the Cambodian government formally halted the project, with no ground works ever started.
lesson: Consent costs less to obtain than to overcome; whoever can physically hold the only access road controls the schedule.
locationRole: Proposed dam site in the Areng valley

title: The Bulacan flood control projects
subtitle: Recorded as finished in 2024. Ground was broken in August 2025.
summary: Investigations in 2024 and 2025 found Philippine flood control works logged as complete that had never been built, including a P96 million riverbank structure at Sipat in Plaridel recorded as finished in 2024 but only started in August 2025. Of the 668 flood control projects Bulacan submitted, 411 sat outside any identified flood hazard zone.
lesson: Paying against a completion report rather than an inspection makes the report, not the structure, the thing being bought.
locationRole: Riverbank works site in Plaridel

title: Thu Thiem New Urban Area
subtitle: The map proving who owned what went missing. Everything after that stalled.
location: Thu Thiem, Ho Chi Minh City
summary: Ho Chi Minh City began clearing a 2,600 hectare peninsula opposite District 1 in 2002 and hired Sasaki Associates to master-plan it in 2003. The authoritative 1996 land-title map vanished from municipal records, leaving compensation impossible to verify against any baseline; the first resettlement certificates arrived around 2023 and in 2026 the city was still failing to auction 3,790 resettlement apartments.
lesson: The record of who owned what is the load-bearing document in any redevelopment; lose it and no amount of design work can proceed.
locationRole: Redevelopment peninsula on the Saigon River

title: The Central Kalimantan peatland project
subtitle: A million hectares of peat swamp drained for rice. It burned instead.
summary: From 1995 Suharto's government drained one million hectares of peat forest for irrigated rice and settled about 15,600 families across 45 units, chasing national rice self-sufficiency. Peat is hyperacidic and drainage made it worse, the 1997 fire season devastated the zone, and the Habibie government cancelled the project in April 1999 after at least $500 million had been spent.
lesson: When your own agronomists record that the soil has extreme limitations, that is the finding, not an obstacle to manage around.
locationRole: Drained peat zone and settlement units

title: Ofo
subtitle: Two point two billion dollars raised, and a city of abandoned bicycles.
summary: Started in December 2014 by members of the Peking University cycling club, Ofo raised $2.2 billion and reached a $3 billion valuation, putting dockless bikes across China and into Singapore, Paris and other cities. Rental income never covered deployment, maintenance and loss, merger talks with Mobike and DiDi failed, and by 2019 the company had shed most of its staff while hundreds of thousands of users never recovered their deposits.
lesson: Growth funded by user deposits is a liability wearing the costume of traction; prove one unit pays for itself before scaling the fleet.
locationRole: Company headquarters

title: Tsinghua Unigroup's chip-cloud project
subtitle: A national semiconductor champion borrowed thirty billion and had to be rescued.
summary: Tsinghua Unigroup, spun out of Tsinghua University, bid $23 billion for Micron in 2015 and then committed roughly $15 billion to a chip-cloud complex in Dongguan. Debt passed $30 billion by 2020, the Dongguan project was abandoned in restructuring, and in April 2022 JAC Capital recapitalised the group with $9.4 billion, ending its independence while subsidiaries such as Yangtze Memory continued.
lesson: Vertical integration bought with debt assumes every layer delivers on time; one slow layer turns the whole structure into a refinancing problem.
locationRole: Group headquarters

title: The Ryugyong Hotel
subtitle: A hundred and five storeys, finished outside, empty for four decades inside.
summary: Construction of the 330 metre, 3,000-room pyramid began in August 1987 with Soviet subsidy and reached full height by 1992 at a cost of roughly $750 million, after which Soviet support ended and the famine years followed. Orascom spent about $180 million on cladding and LED panels in the 2000s, but the interior has never been fitted out and the building now serves as a propaganda screen.
lesson: Finishing the visible shell of a stalled project makes it look resolved and removes the pressure that would have finished it.
locationRole: Unfinished hotel tower

title: Dara Sakor
subtitle: A city for 1.3 million promised inside a national park. One casino opened.
summary: Union Development Group took a concession in 2008 that grew to 45,000 hectares of Botum Sakor National Park, promising an airport, deep-sea port, hospitals and casinos for 1.3 million residents by 2030. Only a casino, hotel and apartments were built, roughly 20% of the park's primary forest was lost, over 1,000 families were displaced, and the United States sanctioned the developer in 2020.
lesson: A concession granted well beyond the legal size limit is a signal that no other rule will bind the project either.
locationRole: Resort concession inside Botum Sakor National Park

title: Byju's
subtitle: The world's most valuable edtech firm shed twenty billion in under two years.
summary: Founded in Bangalore in 2011, Byju's raised about $6 billion and reached a $22 billion valuation in late 2022 on pandemic demand and heavy marketing, including cricket sponsorships worth $19 million. High-pressure selling, churn outpacing acquisition and operating losses above $400 million a year drove the valuation below $2 billion by mid-2024, with insolvency proceedings filed in July and quashed in August.
lesson: Subscriptions sold under pressure produce churn, not a customer base; read renewals before raising on the headline number.
locationRole: Company headquarters

title: SsangYong Motor
subtitle: Two foreign owners, two collapses, one plant that outlived them both.
summary: Korea's last independent mid-tier carmaker fell into crisis when Shanghai Automotive went bankrupt in 2009, triggering 2,646 layoffs and a two-month factory occupation at Pyeongtaek. Mahindra bought 70% in 2011, refused further capital in April 2020 after fifteen straight quarterly losses, and the company entered receivership that December before emerging under KG Group and being renamed KG Mobility in March 2023.
lesson: A parent's balance sheet is part of your capital structure; a subsidiary with no independent cash generation fails when the parent does.
locationRole: Sole assembly plant and headquarters

title: Yamaichi Securities
subtitle: A century of broking, and 265 billion yen parked in the Cayman Islands.
summary: Founded in 1897 and one of Japan's Big Four brokerages, Yamaichi hid about 265 billion yen of client trading losses by transferring them to shell companies in the Cayman Islands and Australia, continuing the practice after regulators banned it around 1991. A magazine exposed the scheme in April 1997, the firm announced its closure that November and dismissed 7,500 staff, and a court declared it bankrupt on 2 June 1999.
lesson: Losses moved off the balance sheet keep compounding; the concealment, not the original trade, sets the size of the eventual failure.
locationRole: Head office in the Tokyo financial district

title: Takata
subtitle: The cheaper propellant worked, until humidity got inside the canister.
summary: Takata, founded in 1933, supplied roughly 15 to 20% of the world's airbag inflators using ammonium nitrate, a cheap propellant its own engineers warned was unstable. Moisture degradation caused inflators to rupture and fire metal fragments at occupants, killing at least 16 people in the United States, forcing recalls of more than 100 million airbags, and ending in Japan's largest postwar bankruptcy in June 2017.
lesson: A component saving is multiplied by every unit shipped, and so is its failure mode; price the recall before choosing the cheaper chemistry.
locationRole: Corporate headquarters

title: Mt. Gox
subtitle: Seventy percent of the world's bitcoin trades, run out of hot wallets.
summary: Started as a trading post for Magic cards and repurposed for bitcoin in July 2010, Mt. Gox under Mark Karpeles handled roughly 70% of global bitcoin transactions from an office in Shibuya. It held customer coins in internet-connected hot wallets with no multi-signature control or malleability protection, and in February 2014 declared about 850,000 bitcoin missing, worth some $450 million, before filing for bankruptcy.
lesson: Custody is a different business from trading and needs controls that assume the operator's own systems are already compromised.
locationRole: Exchange offices in Shibuya

title: Saigon One Tower
subtitle: A skeleton on the riverfront, given a glass skin and still nobody inside.
summary: Begun in 2007 on the Saigon River at 34A Ton Duc Thang Street with about $228 million financed by Dong A Bank, the 195 metre tower stopped in 2012 when Vietnam's property market contracted, leaving a bare concrete frame in the centre of the city. A dragon-scale glass facade was fitted in September 2022, but by 2026 the building held no tenants and its ownership and legal status remained unresolved.
lesson: Cosmetic progress on a stalled asset restores the appearance of value without touching the title and debt that stopped it.
locationRole: Unfinished tower on the Saigon riverfront

title: The Hopewell Project
subtitle: A thousand concrete pillars across Bangkok, and no railway on top of them.
summary: Thailand's cabinet approved a 60.1 kilometre elevated road and rail system through Bangkok on 9 November 1990 for 80 billion baht, with no feasibility study, in partnership with Hong Kong's Hopewell Holdings. Work reached only 10 to 13% before the 1997 baht collapse ended financing, the cabinet terminated the scheme in 1998, and over 1,000 pillars nicknamed Thailand's Stonehenge were left standing while litigation ran on for decades.
lesson: Skipping the feasibility study does not save time; it moves the cost of finding out into concrete that has already been poured.
locationRole: Elevated corridor from Hua Lamphong to Don Mueang

title: Taiwan's hard disk drive ventures
subtitle: Five companies, one state blueprint, and not one surviving drive maker.
summary: From 1986 Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute transferred disk drive designs to five ventures at Hsinchu, among them Taiwan Priam, Microscience, Magtron, Greenery Technology and Zentek. Taiwan Priam beat American yields at 77% but sold fewer than 500 units domestically, and every venture had failed by 1999, unable to reach the volumes that won larger rivals supplier priority and pricing.
lesson: In a consolidated supply chain, scale is the precondition for good manufacturing rather than its reward; low volume buys the worst prices.
locationRole: Manufacturing sites in Hsinchu Science Park

title: Xiong'an New Area
subtitle: Complete infrastructure, dark windows, and a rail station running near empty.
summary: Announced in April 2017 as the new area that would relieve Beijing, Xiong'an built full infrastructure and a high-speed station sized for about 100,000 passengers a day. By 2025 the roughly 120,000 people housed there were largely locals rehoused from demolished villages rather than inbound migrants, independent estimates put vacancy between 30% and 70%, and retail units on Wanda Golden Street carried no transfer fee at all.
lesson: Building the city first assumes people follow buildings; they follow work, and no decree reverses that order.
locationRole: Planned new area southwest of Beijing
